summary: Miqyas logged 66 articles across the full seven days from October 17 to 23. Social coverage carried the heaviest negative share at 28.8% (19 of 66), followed by political at 21.2% (14) and economic at 10.6% (7). All three negative shares fell well below the previous week (October 10 to 16), when social reached 53%, political 34% and economic 19%. The social negatives this week cluster around violence and custody: the abduction of 20 police recruits in Mastung, an army major killed by a roadside bomb in Gwadar district, and two cases in which the main suspects in high-profile deaths (the Multan orphan case and the Laiba Ijaz case) were killed by gunfire while in police hands, in accounts given by police and the Crime Control Department that remain unverified. Lahore topping a global pollution ranking on October 23 added to the tally late in the week.

The dominant storyline was the dispute about governor's rule and the emergency imposed on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11. Eight of the week's 13 flagged stories trace back to it: ministers trading barbs with JUI-F chief Fazlur Rehman, the government declining Mahmood Achakzai's request for a neutral venue for talks, Bilawal Bhutto Zardari saying the measures could end if the opposition backs a joint counterterrorism plan, the Peshawar High Court taking up PTI's petitions that call the measures unconstitutional, Achakzai asking the government to disclose where KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has been, PTI setting preconditions for talks, PM's adviser Rana Sanaullah warning that parties not backing the fight against terrorism would be 'minus', and a public rift inside PTI itself, with Ali Amin Gandapur demanding an apology from Salman Akram Raja after the party's protest march. The political negatives reflect a standoff rather than a one-off event: each side set conditions for talks this week, and by their own accounts none of those conditions were met.

Economic coverage was the most neutral of the three categories (75.8% neutral) and the only one with more positive readings (9) than negative (7). The positives were mostly concrete: a petrol price cut of Rs5.16 per litre on October 20, a new system to manage loadshedding, a defence cooperation accord with Turkiye, Qatar and Indonesia, and the Maldives president's state visit. Against that, the same day as the fuel price cut brought a downward revision of GDP growth to 3.65%, short of target, and Jamaat-e-Islami announced a third phase of protests against the petroleum levy starting October 23. JI said a planned meeting with the prime minister stalled after the government stopped contacting it; the report carried no government response, so that remains the party's account only.

On lean and confidence, 62 of 66 articles read as balanced and 4 as pro-government, with none leaning the other way. Two of the four pro-government readings fell inside the KP storyline (Rana Sanaullah's remarks on the talks venue and on parties being 'minus'), in each case because the report carried only the government's side with no reply from PTI or the opposition alliance, a sourcing gap rather than an editorial slant Miqyas could attribute to the publication. Confidence was medium on 43 articles, high on 22 and low on just one: the Achakzai item about Afridi, which Miqyas could only read via an RSS excerpt. Several of the week's gravest stories, including the Mastung abduction, the Gwadar operation and the Laiba Ijaz case, rest wholly on official or police accounts, which is why they sit at medium rather than high confidence even where more than one publication reported matching details.

notableStories.headline: PHC takes up PTI's petitions challenging KP governor's rule, emergency
notableStories.context: The Peshawar High Court began hearing PTI's challenge to the October 11 emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, moving the week's central political dispute into the courts, with no ruling reported yet.

notableStories.headline: Armed men abduct 20 under-training police personnel in Mastung: officials
notableStories.context: Officials said gunmen seized 20 police recruits travelling home on the Quetta-Karachi Highway, the largest security incident in Miqyas's coverage this week, with no group claiming responsibility at the time of reporting.

notableStories.headline: 'We need no loyalty certificates': Gandapur hits back at Salman Akram Raja
notableStories.context: Three publications reported an open feud between two senior PTI figures after the party's protest march, a sign of strain inside the main opposition party while KP is under governor's rule.

notableStories.headline: Multan orphan's prime murder suspect shot dead in alleged encounter after custody escape
notableStories.context: The main suspect in a 14-year-old's death was killed in what the CCD called an exchange of fire after a custody escape police have not explained, one of two custodial deaths in high-profile cases this week.

notableStories.headline: JI to launch third phase of anti-petroleum levy protests from Oct 23
notableStories.context: Jamaat-e-Islami said it would begin a third round of nationwide sit-ins against the petroleum levy, keeping fuel taxation on the political agenda despite a petrol price cut earlier in the week.
